# S3 Object Variables

A `${s3:<bucket>/<key>}` variable reads the content of an Amazon S3 object while the Serverless Framework loads `serverless.yml`. Use it for values kept in a shared bucket, such as a configuration value or a certificate, that several services read.

The following `serverless.yml` sets an environment variable to the content of the `config/api-url.txt` object in the `my-config-bucket` bucket:

```yaml
# serverless.yml
service: my-service

provider:
  name: aws
  runtime: nodejs24.x

functions:
  hello:
    handler: handler.hello
    environment:
      API_URL: ${s3:my-config-bucket/config/api-url.txt}
```

The variable resolves to the object's content as a string, with no parsing. The bucket can be in any Region: requests follow Amazon S3's redirect to the bucket's Region.

## Syntax of the s3 variable

```text
${s3:BUCKET/KEY}
${RESOLVER_NAME:s3:BUCKET/KEY}
${RESOLVER_NAME:s3:s3://BUCKET/KEY}
${RESOLVER_NAME:s3:arn:aws:s3:::BUCKET/KEY}
${RESOLVER_NAME:NESTED_RESOLVER_NAME:KEY}
${RESOLVER_NAME:NESTED_RESOLVER_NAME}
```

- `BUCKET`: the bucket name. Everything after the first `/` is the object key, so keys with `/` work as written.
- `RESOLVER_NAME`: an [AWS resolver](./README.md#configure-an-aws-resolver). `${s3:...}` uses the deployment credentials.
- `NESTED_RESOLVER_NAME`: a nested resolver with `type: s3` that sets the bucket, and optionally the key; see [Set the bucket and key in a resolver](#set-the-bucket-and-key-in-a-resolver).
- Through a resolver, the address can also be an S3 URI (`s3://BUCKET/KEY`) or an S3 object ARN in the `aws` partition (`arn:aws:s3:::BUCKET/KEY`).

When the object doesn't exist, the variable uses its default (`${s3:my-config-bucket/config/api-url.txt, 'https://example.com'}`), otherwise the command stops with a `Cannot resolve '${s3:...}' variable` error. Other errors, such as a missing bucket or denied access, stop the command even when a default is set.

## Permissions for s3 variables

The credentials that read the object need `s3:GetObject` on it. Grant `s3:ListBucket` on the bucket too when a variable has a default: without it, Amazon S3 answers a request for a missing object with `AccessDenied` instead of `NoSuchKey`, and `AccessDenied` stops the command. See the [GetObject permissions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/API/API_GetObject.html).

## Read objects with another account or profile

To read an object with other credentials, declare an [AWS resolver](./README.md#configure-an-aws-resolver) and reference `s3` through it:

```yaml
stages:
  default:
    resolvers:
      sharedAccount:
        type: aws
        profile: shared-account

provider:
  name: aws

functions:
  hello:
    handler: handler.hello
    environment:
      API_URL: ${sharedAccount:s3:my-config-bucket/config/api-url.txt}
      LOGO_URL: ${sharedAccount:s3:s3://my-config-bucket/config/logo-url.txt}
```

This service also deploys with the `shared-account` profile: a single `type: aws` resolver supplies the deployment credentials when neither `provider.profile` nor `provider.resolver` is set. To deploy with other credentials, set `provider.profile`, or declare another `type: aws` resolver and name it in `provider.resolver`.

## Set the bucket and key in a resolver

To name the bucket once, declare a nested resolver with `type: s3` and `bucketName`; the variable's address is then the object key. With `objectKey` set as well, the variable needs no address:

```yaml
stages:
  default:
    resolvers:
      sharedAccount:
        type: aws
        configBucket:
          type: s3
          bucketName: my-config-bucket
        apiUrlFile:
          type: s3
          bucketName: my-config-bucket
          objectKey: config/api-url.txt

provider:
  name: aws

functions:
  hello:
    handler: handler.hello
    environment:
      LOGO_URL: ${sharedAccount:configBucket:config/logo-url.txt}
      API_URL: ${sharedAccount:apiUrlFile}
```

## S3 resolver settings

A nested resolver with `type: s3` under an AWS resolver accepts these keys:

| Key                    | Type   | Default                          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------- | ------ | -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `type`                 | String | Required                         | `s3`.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `bucketName`           | String | None                             | Bucket to read from. The variable's address is then the object key.                                                                                                                                         |
| `objectKey`            | String | None                             | Object to read. Requires `bucketName`; the variable then needs no address.                                                                                                                                  |
| `region`               | String | The parent AWS resolver's Region | Region for the first request. Applies only when the parent AWS resolver doesn't set `region`; requests follow Amazon S3's redirect to the bucket's Region either way.                                       |
| `serverSideEncryption` | String | None                             | Server-side encryption for objects the Framework writes through the resolver when it is the [Compose state store](../../state.md): `AES256`, `aws:kms` or `aws:kms:dsse`. Reading variables doesn't use it. |

## Encrypt state written through an S3 resolver

When an S3 resolver is the Compose `state` store and the bucket policy requires an encryption header on uploads, set `serverSideEncryption` to the algorithm the policy expects. The Framework then sends it as the `x-amz-server-side-encryption` header when it writes state objects. Reads use the [bucket's default encryption](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/bucket-encryption.html) and need no setting.

The following bucket policy denies uploads without `AES256`:

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "EnforceEncryptionMethod",
      "Effect": "Deny",
      "Principal": "*",
      "Action": "s3:PutObject",
      "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::my-state-bucket/*",
      "Condition": {
        "StringNotEquals": {
          "s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption": ["AES256"]
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Without `serverSideEncryption`, writing state to this bucket stops with an error like:

```text
AccessDenied: User: ... is not authorized to perform: s3:PutObject on resource: "arn:aws:s3:::my-state-bucket/..." with an explicit deny in a resource-based policy
```

The following `serverless-compose.yml` writes state with `AES256`:

```yaml
# serverless-compose.yml
state: stateBucket

stages:
  default:
    resolvers:
      myAccount:
        type: aws
        stateBucket:
          type: s3
          bucketName: my-state-bucket
          serverSideEncryption: AES256

services:
  service-a:
    path: service-a
```
